principle: Evidence informs bounded interface decisions; it never authorizes fabricated claims, dark patterns or universal conversion promises.

rules.claim: Keyboard focus must remain visibly identifiable.

evidence.locator: SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible / 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured

rules.claim: Scarlett may bound very wide prose to improve reading ergonomics while preserving the text itself.

evidence.locator: Width is no more than 80 characters or glyphs for blocks of text

rules.claim: Motion must be purposeful and must respect the user's reduced-motion preference.
Scarlett may visually prioritize a small number of actions that already exist on the source page; it may not invent urgency, scarcity, endorsements or outcomes.

evidence.source: Hick, W. E. (1952), On the rate of gain of information

rules.claim: Important existing interactive targets may receive stronger visual salience without changing their destination or action.

evidence.source: Fitts, P. M. (1954), The information capacity of the human motor system in controlling the amplitude of movement

rules.claim: Trust cues can only be surfaced when they are present and attributable in the source; Scarlett never manufactures social proof or security claims.
